what_it_proves: twin-scene invisibility ladder: an impact against a sleeper must match the awake twin within the sleep quietness bound, and the awake twin must conserve momentum up to the floor's friction budget. R1 red: equal-mass awake impact destroys 85.5 kg*m/s outright (the deeper defect under machine S3); R2/R3 conserved; R4 guards against wake-thrash; R5 is the analytic prover. 2026-08-19, Argus wired and the narration completed: 12 checks became 21, the single R1 failure unchanged. Every rung's verdict was read off VELOCITIES, and a velocity change on a floor with friction has more than one cause. The strike is now GEOMETRIC in both twins: closest approach 0.3944 m against a 0.4000 m contact distance for R1, 0.876 / 0.853 against 0.8504 for R2 / R3. Two more DOFs asserted green in both twins: nothing wanders off the lane (0.00e+00 m -- the strike is along +X and nothing acts north, and a body that left the three-tile floor would have produced velocity readings this test believed), and both bodies ride the floor tiles the whole way (worst departure 4.15e-03 m; a body that sank into or climbed a tile edge is a different experiment from the one the rung names).
gaps: red-first by design until the sleep-awake resolver (task #56) and the equal-mass annihilation RCA land. Omega and orientation are watched and waived by name: D2 owns contact torque and this is INV-31's ladder. One thing the geometry assert taught, recorded because it will bite the next writer: Argus separation is 3D centre-to-centre, and these bodies ride a common floor at very different heights (a 1.2 m castle beside an 0.08 m grain), so the contact distance is the hypotenuse of the half-extent sum and the height difference, NOT the half-extent sum. The flat formula read a 0.9 m/s strike that plainly landed as a 0.23 m miss. The tolerance is derived too: the engine steps physics at 1/30 s while the loop samples at 1/60, so the true closest approach can be missed by one physics step of closing distance.

what_it_proves: the refusal ledger holds what a braced body actually refused. One striker, one KINEMATIC target, airborne so no floor row muddies the accounting: the striker's own momentum delta is the truth, and the book must match it. Measured 1440.2 refused / 1439.2 booked = 99.9%; it was 2.5% before the warm-start and friction doors learned to book. 2026-08-19, Argus wired and the narration completed: 3 asserts became 14, all green, and the run TAUGHT something the narration got wrong first time. The off-axis columns booked_y and booked_z were summed by this test from the very first version and then silently dropped. Y is zero, as predicted. Z is NOT: it holds -132.449 kg*m/s, and that is real and correct. The striker comes to rest against the braced face and slides DOWN it under gravity; the friction resisting the slide is refused exactly as the normal load was. Checked the same way the X column is, against the striker's own delta and no invented value: at the deadline it falls at 5.699 m/s where free fall gives 6.533, and 160 kg times that deficit is 133.4 kg*m/s against 132.449 in the book -- 99%. The Z column is now asserted at that ratio and additionally held inside the Coulomb cone. So the SECOND door of the F1 RCA (the friction block that once booked nothing at all) is proved to book in the right direction and the right amount, which the original test could not say. The strike itself is now geometric rather than inferred: closest approach 0.4915 m against a 0.5000 m half-extent sum, peak closing speed 8.998 m/s against a 9.000 release. And the braced body's refusal is total -- it never moved at any point on any axis (0.00e+00 m), was never spun (0.00e+00 rad/s), and the striker came out square (no lateral drift, no spin: this contact has no lever arm, so zero is the right answer and not D2).
gaps: linear only; angular refusals are not booked at all (the angular side has no door yet), and this geometry cannot expose that gap because a square centred strike has no lever arm to refuse. An off-centre strike against a braced body is the experiment that would. The striker's vz and z are waived by name in the narration: it is airborne with gravity on, deliberately, because the fall is what keeps a floor row out of the accounting.
